topic.title: Project Roles
topic.shortdesc: Project roles determine how the project's users access and manage the project.

body.p: Project access is determined by project visibility (public or private) and by each user's role in the project. Project roles are scoped to a project and are separate from platform user roles, although the platform user role of a user decides which project roles are available to them. Users with the platform user role of Author or Contributor can be given a project role (the Subject Matter Expert platform user role is not compatible with project roles).
There are three project roles, Collaborator, Maintainer, and Owner. Each role includes all privileges granted by the preceding role.

section.title: Collaborator
section.p: Collaborator is the project role for users who propose changes to the project without changing it themselves. This is the only project role available to users with the Contributor platform user role. Users with the Author platform user role can be assigned this role in private projects only.

li.p: Read the content of the project.
Edit the project files in their own personal workspace.
Create review tasks from the changes in their workspace.
Participate in the project's review tasks.

section.p: Collaborators cannot commit to the project, integrate review tasks, or publish deliverables. The review tasks they create remain without an owner until a project maintainer or owner takes ownership of them.

section.title: Maintainer
section.p: Maintainer is the project role for users who work on the project content. This project role is available to users with the Author platform user role.
In addition to what Collaborators can do, users with the Maintainer role can:

li.p: Commit their changes to the project.
Own the review tasks of the project and integrate the accepted changes.
Manage the branches, publications, and deliverables of the project.

section.p: Maintainers cannot access the Members and Settings pages of the project, and cannot add new members.

section.title: Owner
section.p: Owner is the role assigned to the user who created the project or to users who were granted this role by another project owner. This project role is available to users with the Author platform user role. In addition to what Maintainers can do, users with the Owner role has additional administrative privileges related to managing the project.
For example, the project owner can:

li.p: Access the Settings page to configure project settings.
Access the Members page to add or remove project members (for private projects).
Assign project roles to other users.

section.title: Which Users Can Hold Each Role
section.p: A user's platform user role limits the project roles they can be assigned. Users with the Subject-Matter Expert platform user role cannot hold any project role.

row.entry: Contributors, in any project. Authors, in private projects only.
Authors, in private projects. In public projects, all the Authors of the organization have this level of access automatically.

section.title: Project Membership and Visibility
section.p: How a user receives a project role depends on the project visibility:

li.p: Public projects - All users with the Author platform user role automatically have access to the project, with the privileges of a Maintainer. Users with the Contributor platform user role do not: a project owner must add them to the project as Collaborators.
Private projects - Only users explicitly invited by a project owner can access the project. The project owner controls the list of project members and each member's role.

section.p: To manage the members of a project and their roles, see the Members page.
